explanation: Pair 1 with 100, 2 with 99 and so on: that gives 50 pairs that each make 101. The young Carl Friedrich Gauss is said to have spotted this shortcut at school.

claims.text: The sum of the whole numbers from 1 to 100 is 5,050.
1,000 and 5,000 fall short of the true total of 5,050, and 10,100 is double it.
The whole numbers from 1 to 100 form 50 pairs that each sum to 101.
A well-known story says the young Carl Friedrich Gauss found this shortcut at school.
